chunks: And I asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bathing) without a waist-covering where no one sees him.
He said: “There is no harm in it.”
183 - And he said, and he was asked:
About a man who has intercourse with a woman but does not ejaculate: is ghusl obligatory upon him?
He said: ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “When the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, then ghusl has become obligatory.”

key_terms.الْخِتَانُ: the circumcised part; used here as a legal expression for intercourse
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: the ritual bath made obligatory in certain states
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.يُصِيبُ الْمَرْأَةَ: has sexual relations with the woman

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required after intercourse without ejaculation, and may one bathe without a covering when alone?
ai.summary: This hadith gives two legal rulings regarding ghusl. First, there is no harm in a man performing ghusl without an izar when he is alone and unseen; second, ghusl becomes obligatory through sexual intercourse itself, even if ejaculation does not occur.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: I asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bathing) without a covering (loincloth) when no one can see him.
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُ اَلْمَرْأَةَ فَلاَ يُنْزِلُ أَ عَلَيْهِ غُسْلٌ
قَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ «إِذَا مَسَّ اَلْخِتَانُ اَلْخِتَانَ فَقَدْ وَجَبَ اَلْغُسْلُ.
